why: APPEND-ONLY, WRITTEN BY A HUMAN, VERIFIED BY THE BUILD. `fingerprints.json` digests the computed VALUES so a vendor release that changes what a number IS cannot pass unseen — but that defence had one hole, and it was the ordinary workflow: the regeneration is part of taking the release. Install, regenerate, commit, green. Measured, not argued: an inverted-weight `wma`, 2.1% wrong against its own fixture, was planted and the artefacts regenerated the way a release arrives, and every check reported passing. So the digest gets the rule an id already has in renames.json. The generator can see that a number moved; it CANNOT see whether the vendor fixed a defect or shipped one, and those two have opposite consequences for every chart drawn from it. It refuses to write until somebody writes which, here. Nothing is ever deleted from this list: the chain from an indicator's first digest to its current one is how a reader knows what its numbers have been through.
form: Each entry is one indicator moving once: `id`, `from` (the digest on file), `to` (the digest this run derives), `encoding` (which spelling those two digests are written in — a digest compared across spellings measures nothing), `reason` (what changed and how it was confirmed — a sentence, not `vendor update`), and `settles` when the retroactive window moved with it. Entries for one id, within one encoding, chain: each `from` is the `to` of the one before it.
encodingForm: THE OTHER KIND OF CHANGE, AND IT IS NOT A VALUE. Re-spelling how a reading is written down moves EVERY digest in `fingerprints.json` at once while no indicator computes anything different, so declaring it above would be three hundred false statements — and waving it through would be the widest laundering channel in the file. It is declared here instead, ONCE: `from` (the identity the committed file carries), `to` (the identity this run encodes with) and `reason`. While an identity holds, every digest answers for itself exactly as before; when it moves and this chain says why, the whole file is re-derived and no per-id reason is asked for, because no value moved. An identity that moved with nothing here is refused. This chain is append-only too, and each `from` is the `to` of the one before it.

encodings.reason: The encoding had no name, so a change to it could not be declared and would have arrived as three hundred undeclared value moves — indistinguishable from a vendor rewriting three hundred indicators. Naming it is the whole of this entry: `v1` IS the spelling every committed digest below was already taken over, `String(value)` per finite reading, and this run re-derived all 310 of them byte-identical to what was on file. Not one number moved.
